To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

mice lacking rod α transducins (Gnat1), cone-specific cyclic nucleotide gated (CNG) channels (Cnga3), and melanopsin photopigment (Opn4) retain a functional rod opsin-based photoreceptive mechanism that is capable of driving widespread visual responses throughout the mammalian visual pathway.
mice lacking rod, cone and melanopsin phototransduction can still respond to light in the ERG.

mice lacking all three known phototransduction mechanisms in the mammalian retina retain a functional photoreception pathway, and that this pathway is based on rod opsin and Gnat2, but is independent of Gnat1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms underlying visual perception.
the development of new therapies for inherited retinal diseases.
the visual system of mice with mutations in genes that code for proteins involved in light sensing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TKO mouse is not completely blind.
the TKO mice are functionally blind.

the visual system of Gnat1−/-;Cnga3-/-;Opn4-/- mice is not blind, but instead is capable of light detection via rod phototransducin-independent mechanisms, and is able to support visual responses in a wide range of brain regions, including the visual cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Gnat1−, Cnga3− and Opn4− mice have a light response in the retina that is mediated by rod opsin.
we found an unexpected visual response in a mouse lacking all three known visual transduction cascades.
the Gnat1−/-;Cnga3-/-;Opn4-/- mice are not blind, as previously assumed, and they have a functional rod photoreceptor system, which is not dependent on the canonical G-protein signaling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rod phototransducer knockout mice are not necessarily blind.
the visual system is much more robust than one would expect based on the known components of retinal phototransduction cascades.
there are still many mysteries in the field of photoreception and vision.
